A small interface for a complicated command

A durable command may lock rows, update product state, insert or cancel queue jobs, classify constraint failures, and preserve idempotency. Exposing those mechanics to callers creates a wide interface even when each method is short.

A deeper module accepts the application intent and owns the coordination. Production uses database and queue adapters; tests use fault-injecting adapters at internal seams to prove rollback before and after each effect.

The deletion test is useful: if removing the module would spread transaction rules back across several callers, the module is earning its place. If nothing but forwarding calls reappears, the interface remains shallow.
